hypothesis: Thermal warmup completes before eight-core CPU timing at existing top points and normal return
conclusion: The native CPU control returns normally on port 3-3 and completes every wake sample. Its strict timing expectation fails: one CPU-only run establishes observed maxima, not worst-case bounds or combined-load timing. DMA, GPU and NPU completion timing is unmeasured (budgets 250, 1,000 and 1,000 us).
narrative: Conditions: CPU-L 1794 MHz at 1000 mV, CPU-B 2002 MHz at 1050 mV. Budgets against board maxima: CPU0 timer assertion to C handler entry 50 us against 6.583 us; IRQ-masked or kernel critical region 25 us against 268.125 us; kernel ISR lock acquisition and outer hold 25 us each against 9.042 and 19.792 us; kernel task lock acquisition and outer hold 25 us each against 238.750 and 12.625 us; highest-priority ready task on an idle and a busy core 100 and 250 us against 66.625 and 104.542 us. The two largest overruns precede the top-point workload by 132 ms; the workload itself reaches 62.750 us masked and 73.417 us task-lock wait (core 6).
